option_title: Industrial food ingredient replacement for sustainability
question: Does increasing the capacity of a neural ingredient-substitution model measurably improve its ranking of sustainable replacements, measured as Hit@1 on Recipe1MSubs [src_gismo_sizes]?
hypothesis: More capacity in a substitution ranker improves substitution ranking because larger encoders capture finer ingredient context, as LLM results suggest [src_llm].
held_fixed: Recipe1MSubs benchmark and its 10,747-sample test split
Contrastive loss, Adam optimizer, early stopping on validation MRR
5 seeds per width, ranking over the full vocabulary, MRR and Hit@k metrics

predictions.if_lever: Hit@1 rises with width, reaching at least 22 percent at width 512, above GISMo's 20.56, and still climbing.
predictions.if_not: Hit@1 plateaus near GISMo's 20.56 at every width; extra capacity adds nothing, so wider models are not the lever.
predictions.decision_rule: Compute is the lever if Hit@1 at width 512 minus Hit@1 at width 64 is at least 2.0 points and exceeds twice the pooled standard error; otherwise it is not.
predictions.noise_rule: Five seeds per width, mean and standard deviation reported; a real effect must exceed twice the pooled standard deviation, and GISMo's reported Hit@1 spread is 0.14 points.
predictions.expected_why: Published LLM fine-tuning lifted Hit@1 on this benchmark family from 34.53 to 38.03, so larger encoders should lift it here too [src_llm].

compute_tested_why: The test varies the ranker's embedding width, which sets model size and per-step FLOPs; wider models need more GPU memory and compute, so more GPUs buy the larger widths.
scored_against: Measured Hit@1 and MRR at each width are compared with GISMo's published 20.56 and 31.51 and the LT+Freq baseline's 18.10 and 27.66; a correct setup reproduces them within tolerance first.

arms.what: GISMo-style GIN ranker trained at embedding widths 64, 128, 256, 512 (the compute axis)
Optional stretch: a small pretrained transformer encoder with the GISMo scoring head, if the width sweep plateaus

baseline.what: LT+Freq statistical baseline (strongest non-neural): test MRR 27.66, Hit@1 18.10

anchor.what: Reproduce GISMo's published test-set MRR of 31.51 and Hit@1 of 20.56 using the official code, within 2 MRR points [src_gismo_gismo].
anchor.tolerance: plus or minus 2.0 MRR points (mean over 5 seeds)

checks: Downloaded splits contain 49,044 / 10,729 / 10,747 samples as published.
Ranking is over the 6,653-ingredient vocabulary, matching GISMo.
Anchor mean MRR lands within 2 points of 31.51 before the sweep starts.
Per-width results averaged over 5 seeds; a real gap exceeds twice the pooled standard deviation.
Best width re-evaluated on the high-footprint source-ingredient subset.

phases.what: Download Recipe1MSubs, FlavorGraph, and the gismo code; verify split counts; build the high-footprint ingredient list.
phases.stop_rule: Stop if the test split does not contain 10,747 samples.

phases.what: Reproduce GISMo: 5 training runs on one A100, timed.
phases.stop_rule: Stop after 5 runs or 12 GPU-hours, whichever comes first.

gate.else: halve the sweep to widths 64 and 128 with 3 seeds each and re-check the budget

phases.what: Train the ranker at widths 64, 128, 256, 512 with 5 seeds each (20 runs) on 4 A100s; measure Hit@1 and MRR.
phases.stop_rule: Stop after 20 runs or 10 wall-clock hours.

phases.what: Evaluate the best width on test tuples whose source ingredient is high-footprint (butter, egg, milk, cream, beef, pork, chicken, cheese, oil).
Optional: fine-tune a small pretrained transformer encoder with the GISMo scoring head, if the width sweep plateaus.

restructuring.sequential_part: Each training run waits on its own gradient epochs, roughly 30 per run; the runs themselves are independent.

scope_gap: The benchmark is home cooking, not industrial formulations; a real replacement needs a lifecycle footprint model and sensory validation, which this test does not buy.
Correct substitution ranking is not the same as a sustainable replacement; the test never measures emissions or production cost.

novelty.closest_prior: Rita 2024 fine-tuned GPT-3.5 and TinyLlama on Recipe1MSubs, lifting Hit@1 from 34.53 to 38.03; no capacity sweep within one protocol exists [src_llm].
novelty.left_open: Whether ranking quality keeps rising with model capacity inside one fixed protocol on Recipe1MSubs is unmeasured; the only scaling evidence is cross-protocol.

limits: Shows ranking accuracy on home recipes, not industrial formulations, and never measures actual environmental footprint or sensory quality of the substitute.
test_summary: Reproduce GISMo's Recipe1MSubs result, then train the ranker at four widths 64, 128, 256, 512 with five seeds each on four GPUs; if Hit@1 climbs past the 20.56 baseline with width, compute is the lever.
